clue.text: Believe in the proposed route, say, in passing

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is to be spoken, giving a sound-alike rather than its spelling

parts.note: to buy something is to believe it, so accepting the suggested road is to buy the way

explanation.surface: Someone casually mentions that they trust the planned route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks the sound-alike: BUY THE WAY spoken gives the phrase entered.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom introducing an incidental remark, a passing aside.

clue.text: Plans turn up in unsolicited mail

indicators.note: in a down light, turning up reads the word for plans from bottom to top

parts.note: maps are plans, as of a town or building

explanation.surface: Unwanted proposals arrive in a pile of junk mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn up' reverses MAPS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrequested bulk email is commonly called by this name, after a canned meat.

clue.text: Originally, young person's chess mainly played in the mind

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are moved around as in a game
originally points to the opening letters of the two following words
mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

explanation.surface: A youngster's chess game is mostly played in their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' gives Y and P; 'mainly' trims CHESS to CHES; 'played' rearranges YPCHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Psyche is a term from Greek for the soul or human mental life, the mind.

clue.text: Spot, a bit like a mountain lake

parts.note: a tarn is a small lake in a mountain corrie
the suffix -ish means somewhat like, as in reddish

explanation.surface: A small blemish resembles a mountain lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' is a verb here: to sully or stain.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot a reputation or surface is to stain or sully it, a synonym.

clue.text: Cob surprising hunt with zeal

indicators.note: surprising suggests an unexpected arrangement of the letters of hunt and zeal

explanation.surface: A surprising and enthusiastic chase after a horse or swan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cob' looks like a horse or a male swan; here it is a kind of nut. 'surprising' rearranges HUNT and ZEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A cob or cobnut is a type of hazel, so its nut is an example.

clue.text: Following a break one follows the smell

definitions.text: Following a break one follows the smell

parts.words: Following a break one follows the smell
parts.note: after a prison break, an animal is brought in to trail the escaped convict by scent

explanation.walkthrough: 'break' reads as a rest, but it is an escape from jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent-trailing hound used by police to follow fugitives fits the described role.

clue.text: In charge, following most of prison's medical unit

indicators.note: following puts the in-charge abbreviation after the prison piece
most of means the word for prison loses its last letter

parts.note: clink is slang for a prison

explanation.surface: The prison's medical unit is under someone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the prison slang word's last letter, and 'following' sets the abbreviation for in charge after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical establishment for outpatient treatment.

clue.text: Staff officer's initial impressions: "I am spy possibly in conferences"

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged in another way
initial impressions means the first letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A staff officer jots first impressions: claims to be a spy at meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial impressions' gives S and O, and 'possibly' rearranges them with IAMSPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Symposia are academic meetings, the plural of symposium.

clue.text: When first of primroses appears in a covering of seeds?

indicators.note: appears in places the initial of primroses inside the seed coat

parts.note: an aril is a fleshy covering on some seeds

indicators.note: first of takes just the opening letter of primroses

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders at what time primroses emerge from their seed casing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' is the definition: April, the month primroses bloom, answers it.
explanation.definitionFit: A month answers the question of when something happens, as a time.

clue.text: Medicine man, two-thirds a fake

indicators.note: two-thirds keeps four of the six letters of the medicine man's word

parts.note: a shaman is a tribal healer or medicine man

explanation.surface: A medicine man is mostly a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a pretence or imposter, the same as a fake.

clue.text: Patronise, deceive and go down

parts.note: to con is to deceive or swindle
to descend is to go down

explanation.surface: Someone talks down to people, tricks them and sinks low.
explanation.definitionFit: To patronise is to treat with condescension, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bandage was altered on article

indicators.note: altered says the letters of was are changed in order

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A dressing was changed on an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altered' rearranges the clue's 'was' to SWA, and 'on' sets it before the article.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap in bandages or cloth, to bind up.

clue.text: One less than this number and one does not get to bat

definitions.text: One less than this number and one does not get to bat

parts.words: One less than this number and one does not get to bat
parts.note: a cricket team has eleven batters, so the substitute beyond them never bats

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a side fields eleven players; the extra squad member, a substitute fielder, does not bat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket squad member beyond the playing eleven acts as substitute fielder and never bats.

clue.text: Period at end of this punishment?

definitions.meaning: a full stop, called a period in America, ends a grammatical unit of words
a penalty passed on a convicted criminal by a judge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' reads as a stretch of time, as in a jail term, but is the full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's sentence is the punishment imposed; grammatically, a full stop ends one.

clue.text: Unit working in the Seychelles and New York in effective cooperation with others

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles

indicators.note: working in places the unit of work inside the place abbreviations

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work or energy

explanation.surface: A unit operates in the Seychelles and New York with good teamwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working in' puts ERG inside the second abbreviation, NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synergy is combined action producing more than the parts alone, effective joint working.

clue.text: Gone to ground but this is kind and helpful

indicators.note: gone suggests the letters have gone awry, rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal has gone to ground, yet this is a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone' looks like part of a phrase about a fox hiding, but it is the signal to rearrange TO GROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: A good turn is a helpful favour or kind deed done for someone.

clue.text: Aid must flow to this sporting venue

indicators.note: flow suggests the letters move and settle in a new order

explanation.surface: Relief supplies should be sent to a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flow' rearranges AID MUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is an arena where sports events are held.

clue.text: Maybe buy it — about a pound — mainly to show popularity

indicators.note: about places the trimmed money word inside the rearranged letters
maybe says the letters of buy it could be ordered otherwise
mainly drops the last letter of the money word

parts.note: quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Perhaps buy it for around a pound, mostly, to prove it is popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges 'buy it' into UBITY; 'mainly' drops the last letter of the British slang for a pound; 'about' wraps the result around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ubiquity is being found everywhere, a sign of widespread popularity.

clue.text: A dentist might, as a temporary measure

definitions.meaning: a dentist fills a hole in a tooth, plugging the space
a makeshift substitute used until something better comes

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the answer is what a dentist does to a cavity.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary fix filling in until a proper solution arrives.

clue.text: Main part of a resort

parts.note: main means the sea, so the part of the town facing the ocean

explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' reads as chief, but it is an old word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The promenade area of a coastal town bordering the ocean fits the description.

clue.text: Improve Scripture in National Curriculum during "English hour"

indicators.note: during puts the curriculum piece inside the English hour letters
in places the scripture letters inside the curriculum letters

parts.note: NC stands for the National Curriculum, the English school syllabus
RI is religious instruction, the school subject of scripture

explanation.surface: Schools enhance scripture lessons within the curriculum's English period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'during' nest the pieces. RI, religious instruction, is the British school subject covering scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich is to make richer or better, to improve.

clue.text: Celebrity getting substantial cover in court

parts.note: big means large or substantial
British judges and barristers wear wigs in court

explanation.surface: A famous person gets big coverage in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' reads as press coverage, but it is the headgear worn by British judges and barristers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is an important or famous person, a celebrity.

clue.text: Cheekily made delivery, we hear, and left unknown

indicators.note: we hear signals the word is chosen for its spoken sound, not spelling

parts.note: in cricket, a bowler who has made a delivery has bowled
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: Someone delivered something cheekily and left without being identified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' gives BOLD from BOWLED, the cricket term for delivering the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Boldly means with audacity or forwardness, cheekily.

clue.text: Real and patchy — crudely typical!

indicators.note: crudely suggests the letters are roughly reworked

explanation.surface: Something genuine but uneven is crudely representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crudely' rearranges REAL and PATCHY.
explanation.definitionFit: Archetypal means being a perfect example, the most typical of its kind.

clue.text: Gave a lesson reportedly on "tense"

indicators.note: reportedly means a word is chosen for how it is spoken aloud

parts.note: a teacher who gave a lesson taught

explanation.surface: A teacher gave a lesson on verb tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' reads as the grammar term, but means stretched tight.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut means tightly stretched, tense like a drawn rope.

clue.text: Kind face

definitions.meaning: a typeface, a design of printed letters

explanation.definitionFit: A type is a sort, and in printing a typeface or font is a face.

clue.text: University position but not for the rest

definitions.text: University position but not for the rest

parts.words: University position but not for the rest
parts.note: a professorship takes its name from a seat, though this one is not for sitting at ease

explanation.walkthrough: A professor holds a named seat in a university; normally that piece of furniture is for resting.
explanation.definitionFit: A professorship at a university is called by the name of a seat of office.

clue.text: One giving conventional treatment cut into a thin piece

indicators.note: into places the word for cut inside the thin strip

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A doctor cuts a thin slice.
explanation.walkthrough: Allopathy is mainstream medicine, as opposed to homeopathy.
explanation.definitionFit: An allopath practises orthodox medicine, the conventional treatment opposed to homeopathy.
